column6: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
column9: The absolutive is the unmarked case in Kakataibo. Both full NPs and pronouns in P function bear no case marker.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
column9: Pronouns follow tripartite alignment: A==(a)n, S==x, P=∅. This is NOT ergative alignment (S and P are not treated alike).

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
column9: Same as 1st person: tripartite alignment on pronouns. S and P are not treated alike.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
column9: Same as 1st and 2nd person: tripartite alignment on pronouns.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
column9: Full NPs follow ergative alignment: A marked with =(a)n / =nën (ERG), S and P unmarked (ABS).

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
column9: No aspect-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies regardless of aspect.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
column9: No aspect-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies regardless of aspect.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
column9: No tense-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies regardless of tense.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
column9: No tense-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies regardless of tense.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
column9: No mood-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies regardless of mood.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
column9: No mood-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies regardless of mood.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
column9: No realis/irrealis split is documented for case marking. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies in realis contexts.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
column9: No realis/irrealis split is documented for case marking. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies in irrealis contexts.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
column9: No agentivity-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies with agentive A.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
column9: No agentivity-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies with non-agentive A.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
column9: No topicality-based split in basic case marking. Note: §16.5 documents discourse-level variation where NPs may follow tripartite alignment, but the default is ergative.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
column9: No topicality-based split in basic case marking. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies with non-topical A.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
column9: No animacy-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies with animate A.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
column9: No animacy-based split is documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies with inanimate A.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
column9: Ergative alignment on full NPs is documented in main clauses.

column6: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
column9: Ergative alignment on full NPs also applies in dependent/nominalized clauses.

column6: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
column9: §16.5 documents discourse-level variation where NPs may follow tripartite alignment if referring to previously introduced topics.

column6: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
column9: Yes. The marker =(a)n expresses ergative, genitive, instrumental, and temporal locative functions (multifunctional marker).

column6: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
column9: Yes for instrumental: =(a)n marks both ergative and instrumental. No for comitative: comitative has distinct markers -bë(ton) and -këñun.
